stem: Structure and bonding can be used to explain many of the properties of substances.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Copper, ice, silicon(IV) oxide, iodine and sodium chloride are all crystalline solids.

Complete the table with:
• the name of a type of bonding found in each crystalline solid,
• the type of lattice structure for each crystalline solid.

| crystalline solid | type of bonding | type of lattice structure |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| ice |  |  |

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Name the strongest type of intermolecular force in ice.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Draw a fully labelled diagram of two water molecules in ice, showing the force in **(i)** and how it forms.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: The graph represents how the temperature of a sample of copper (melting point $1085^{\circ}\text{C}$) changes as it is gradually cooled from $1200^{\circ}\text{C}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Identify the state(s) of matter present during each stage of the process shown in the graph.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State what is happening to the energy and movement of the particles in the copper during stage $\mathbf{X}$.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why the temperature stays constant at $T_1$ during stage $\mathbf{Y}$.
